goal: Half-year sales review of data/orders.json (Jan-Jun 2026): totals, regional breakdowns, top customers, monthly trend, refund behaviour by category, and product-level insights.

steps.title: Half-year totals and status mix
steps.instructions:
DEFINITIONS (use exactly): order revenue = quantity * unit_price. GROSS revenue = sum over ALL 400 orders regardless of status. NET revenue = sum over orders with status=='completed' only. AOV = NET revenue / number of completed orders.

Report for the whole Jan-Jun 2026 file, one line each, in this exact order and format:
TOTAL_ORDERS: <int>
COMPLETED: <int>
REFUNDED: <int>
CANCELLED: <int>
GROSS_REVENUE: <number rounded to 2 decimals>
NET_REVENUE: <number rounded to 2 decimals>
AOV: <number rounded to 2 decimals>
UNITS_COMPLETED: <int, sum of quantity over completed orders>

Write plain numbers with no currency symbol and no thousands separators.

Use the aggregation tools; never add up raw order rows by hand. Copy numbers exactly as the tools print them (do not pad or re-round).

steps.title: Regional breakdown of net revenue
steps.instructions:
DEFINITIONS: order revenue = quantity * unit_price. NET revenue counts ONLY orders with status=='completed'.

For each of the 4 regions compute NET revenue, the number of completed orders, average order value (net revenue / completed orders) and the share of total net revenue in percent. Rank regions by NET revenue descending.

Output exactly 5 lines, numbers rounded to 2 decimals, no currency symbols:
<rank>. <REGION>: revenue=<x>, orders=<int>, aov=<x>, share=<x>%
(4 such lines, then)
LEADER: <REGION>

Example of the line format: '1. FOO: revenue=1234.5, orders=12, aov=102.88, share=30.12%'

Use the aggregation tools; never add up raw order rows by hand. Copy numbers exactly as the tools print them (do not pad or re-round).

steps.title: Top customers by net revenue
steps.instructions:
DEFINITIONS: order revenue = quantity * unit_price. NET revenue counts ONLY orders with status=='completed'.

Rank all customers by NET revenue descending and report the top 5, plus the combined share of those top 5 against the TOTAL net revenue of all customers.

Output exactly 6 lines, numbers rounded to 2 decimals:
<rank>. <customer_id>: revenue=<x>, completed_orders=<int>
(5 such lines, then)
TOP5_SHARE: <x>%

Use the customer_id exactly as it appears in the data (e.g. C012).

steps.title: Monthly net revenue trend with month-over-month change
steps.instructions:
DEFINITIONS: order revenue = quantity * unit_price. NET revenue counts ONLY orders with status=='completed'. Month = first 7 characters of the date field (YYYY-MM).

For each month from 2026-01 to 2026-06 report NET revenue, completed order count, and month-over-month change in percent versus the previous month ((cur - prev) / prev * 100). January has no previous month.

Output exactly 8 lines, numbers rounded to 2 decimals:
<YYYY-MM>: revenue=<x>, orders=<int>, mom=<x>%
(for 2026-01 use mom=n/a; 6 such lines, then)
BEST_MONTH: <YYYY-MM>
WORST_MONTH: <YYYY-MM>

BEST/WORST are by net revenue.

Use the aggregation tools; never add up raw order rows by hand. Copy numbers exactly as the tools print them (do not pad or re-round).

steps.title: Refund behaviour by category
steps.instructions:
DEFINITIONS: order revenue = quantity * unit_price. Refund rate for a group = (number of orders with status=='refunded' in the group) / (TOTAL number of orders in that group, all statuses) * 100. Refunded revenue = sum of revenue over refunded orders only.

For each of the 4 categories report total order count (all statuses), refunded order count, refund rate %, and refunded revenue. Rank by refund rate descending.

Output exactly 7 lines, numbers rounded to 2 decimals:
<rank>. <category>: orders=<int>, refunded=<int>, rate=<x>%, refunded_revenue=<x>
(4 such lines, then)
OVERALL_REFUND_RATE: <x>%
TOTAL_REFUNDED_REVENUE: <x>
WORST_CATEGORY: <category>

OVERALL_REFUND_RATE is over all 400 orders. WORST_CATEGORY is the one with the highest refund rate.

Use the aggregation tools; never add up raw order rows by hand. Copy numbers exactly as the tools print them (do not pad or re-round).

steps.title: Product-level insights

Rank all products by NET revenue descending. Report the top 5 products, then the single lowest-revenue product, then the product with the most units sold, then net revenue per category.

Output exactly 11 lines, numbers rounded to 2 decimals:
<rank>. <product>: revenue=<x>, units=<int>, orders=<int>, aov=<x>
(5 such lines, then)
LOWEST_REVENUE_PRODUCT: <product> (<x>)
MOST_UNITS_PRODUCT: <product> (<int> units)
CATEGORY_REVENUE: <cat1>=<x>, <cat2>=<x>, <cat3>=<x>, <cat4>=<x>
(the CATEGORY_REVENUE list ordered by net revenue descending, on one line)

Use the aggregation tools; never add up raw order rows by hand. Copy numbers exactly as the tools print them (do not pad or re-round).
